sections.title: Abraham's Religious Heritage and Quranic Foundations
sections.summary: The booklet establishes that Submission (Islam) originates from Abraham's teachings according to the Quran. It identifies four pillars of practice from Abraham: five daily Contact Prayers (Salat), obligatory charity (Zakat), Ramadan fasting, and Hajj pilgrimage. The text claims all prayer positions are specified in the Quran and notes that five prayer times are explicitly named in scripture with specific timing guidelines.

sections.title: Ablution and Preparation for Prayer
sections.summary: The text prescribes the required ablution (ritual purification) before prayer as washing faces, arms to elbows, wiping heads with wet hands, and washing feet to ankles, citing Quran 5:6. It describes a major ablution following sexual activity and introduces the dry ablution (Tayammum) using clean soil when water is unavailable. The text specifies what nullifies ablution: digestive excretions, gas, urine, and sleep.

sections.title: Prayer Positions and Movements
sections.summary: The booklet provides detailed instructions for the physical movements in prayer: facing Mecca, stating intention, raising hands, saying takbir (Allahu Akbar), standing position, reciting Al-Fatihah in Arabic (The Key), bowing (Rukoo'), standing again, prostration (Sujood), sitting position, and second prostration. Each transition requires saying 'Allahu Akbar' and specific glorifications. The author notes that Al-Fatihah's Arabic sounds represent a numerical combination that establishes contact, analogous to a telephone number.

sections.title: Prayer Variations and Group Worship
sections.summary: The booklet describes how the five daily prayers vary by number of units: Dawn (2 units), Noon (4 units), Afternoon (4 units), Sunset (3 units), Night (4 units). It notes these numbers (2-4-4-3-4 = 24434) form a multiple of 19, described as the common denominator of the Quran's code. The Friday congregational prayer replaces the Noon prayer and includes two sermons plus two prayer units. Group prayers allow people to join late and make up missed portions, with only the Imam audible during The Key.
